alternatives.label: Human biology, disease and research methods
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular cell biology, biochemistry, human physiology, genetics and pathology with infection and immunity, pharmacology, laboratory study and neuroscience. General statistics and evidence synthesis support research literacy. This provides substantive biomedical foundations while leaving gaps in specialist histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the prolonged VU research placement.
alternatives.labelReason: Label reflects actual enriched content and weight; qualified substantive response, not degree equivalence or a guaranteed VU research placement.
progression: Life-science gateway precedes laboratory study in Year1; molecular and disease study then develops with methods and the chosen health/data emphasis. Every actual prerequisite and term offering checked separately; no additional formal prerequisite invented.

alternatives.label: Biomedicine, population health and prevention
alternatives.concept: Combines substantial molecular, physiological, genetic and disease study with epidemiology, health psychology, qualitative and quantitative methods, sociology, ethics and communication. It develops a related population-health and prevention direction. General social and economics courses are contextual contributions; a dedicated global-health policy or health-systems programme is not supplied.
alternatives.labelReason: Label reflects actual enriched content and weight; qualified substantive response, not degree equivalence or a guaranteed VU research placement.
alternatives.distinctness: Eight courses differ from the biomedical core route, adding sociology, health psychology, qualitative research, public economics and persuasion while reducing specialist neuroscience, anatomy and mathematical/computational methods.
progression: Life-science gateway precedes laboratory study in Year1; molecular and disease study then develops with methods and the chosen health/data emphasis. Every actual prerequisite and term offering checked separately; no additional formal prerequisite invented.

alternatives.label: Biomedical foundations and data analysis
alternatives.concept: Combines molecular, physiological, genetic and disease foundations with statistics, programming, data analysis, numerical methods and machine learning. Actual medical-image processing and quantitative pharmacology give specific biomedical applications. General computing courses do not guarantee biomedical datasets, and this is not a dedicated omics, bioinformatics or clinical prediction-validation sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: Label reflects actual enriched content and weight; qualified substantive response, not degree equivalence or a guaranteed VU research placement.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses differ from the closest biomedical route and twelve from public health: image processing, deep learning, linear algebra, numerical methods and signal systems displace several pharmacology, neurobehavioral and clinical research elements, materially changing the analytical tools.
progression: Life-science gateway precedes laboratory study in Year1; molecular and disease study then develops with methods and the chosen health/data emphasis. Every actual prerequisite and term offering checked separately; no additional formal prerequisite invented.

selection.assessment: Three substantively related and distinct qualified directions retained after every actual profile and contribution weight was reviewed. Body/disease foundations remain substantial in all three; the public option has epidemiology and actual health psychology, while the data option has actual medical image analysis and quantitative pharmacology. General social/economic/computing courses are bounded contextual or methodological contributions, not specialist biomedical/global-health content. The dedicated global-health generator is rejected; generic sociology/economics do not replace health-systems/policy training. Specialist histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the24ECVUplacement remain explicit gaps.

notes.text: VU requires prescribed molecular and practical study, three restricted 6 EC choices and one 24 EC research thesis alongside 30 EC open minor space. UCR offers related biomedical, prevention and data foundations, with earlier laboratory study, but does not duplicate specialist histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology or the prolonged VU placement. Optional UCR independent research is additional, approval-dependent and outside the displayed 180 EC. Degree equivalence, clinical qualification and admission to a particular master are not established.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Biomedical Sciences studies human health and disease from molecules and cells to organs and populations. Its bachelor combines genetics, cell biology, biochemistry, immunity, anatomy and physiology with research methods and practical work. The third year includes open minor space, a restricted choice and a substantial supervised research thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers three qualified related directions: human biology and disease with research methods; biomedicine and population-health prevention; and biomedical foundations with data analysis. Each retains substantial biological and disease content. General social, economics and computing courses support the chosen emphasis; they do not guarantee specialist biomedical projects. Histology, omics, embryology, dedicated oncology and the prolonged VU research placement remain important gaps.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 108 EC prescribed first- and second-year courses, three separate 6 EC restricted choices, 30 EC open minor space and one 24 EC thesis. The first-listed choices are shown; other minor and thesis options are not stacked. Thesis entry requires all 60 EC from year one and at least 42 EC from year two, an approved project and completed registration. A go/no-go review, scientific report, oral and poster presentations and sufficient research performance apply. The usual first-year study advice threshold is 42 EC, subject to applicable exceptions. Lab safety and the Dutch language test or required remediation are mandatory without extra credit. Programme instruction changed to Dutch in 2026; individual courses may be English.
